rationale: Although the paper is set in the context of Argentina's privatization and 2006 re-nationalization of water services and compares respondents who gained water access with those who did not, water access is an explanatory variable rather than an outcome. The study empirically examines the formation of public beliefs and opinions about privatization (measured on a 1-10 scale) in response to first-hand experience of utility investment versus priming with government propaganda, clearly failing Criterion 4 (wrong outcome, E04).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings of Criterion 2 because the study outcome (Criterion 4) is public beliefs/opinions about privatization on a 1-10 scale rather than a water or sanitation service-access outcome, with prior water gain and propaganda priming serving as explanatory variables for belief formation.

evidence_quotes.quote: Reality Versus Propaganda in the Formation of Beliefs About Privatization
We study beliefs about the benefits of the privatization of water services measured immediately after the 2006 nationalization.
Moreover, the effect of priming subjects with government propaganda against privatization has an effect that almost offsets the effect of gaining water.
